title: Introduce versioned atomic persistence and recovery
description:
Replace the current synchronous/delayed JSON writes with a persistence layer that cannot silently lose or corrupt user data. Introduce a versioned v2 envelope such as `{ schemaVersion, revision, data }`, migrate legacy files once, and keep a timestamped backup before changing their format.

Serialize writes through one queue and commit with temp-file plus atomic rename. Coordinate multiple VS Code windows with an exclusive lock or revision check so a stale process cannot overwrite a newer revision. On malformed JSON, partial writes, unsupported schema versions, or failed migrations, quarantine the bad file, attempt verified backup recovery, and otherwise fail visibly in read-only mode. History must store a bounded summary rather than complete secrets or large bodies.

This task is complete only when lifecycle shutdown flushes safely, all migrations are idempotent, failures are actionable, and tests prove recovery from interruption, corruption, conflict, and legacy data.

checklist.text: Define the versioned envelope, revision semantics, limits, and explicit failure modes
Implement idempotent legacy migrations with pre-migration backups and post-migration validation
Serialize durable writes and commit through a same-directory temporary file plus atomic rename
Add cross-window locking or optimistic revision checks with a visible conflict path
Quarantine corrupt data, verify backups before restore, and fall back to a non-destructive read-only state
Migrate history to bounded, secret-free summaries and enforce retention and payload limits
Flush or cancel queued work safely during disposal and extension shutdown
Test migration, concurrent writers, interrupted writes, corruption, backup recovery, limits, and lifecycle shutdown
